name: Thermostats and thermal fuses
summary: Thermostats, thermal switches and one-shot thermal fuses that react to temperature.
uses: Temperature control for incubators, coolers and dehydrators
Overheat protection for heaters and motors
Replacing blown thermal fuses in kettles and dryers
identify: Small round bimetal discs (KSD301) on heaters, kettles, irons and dryers; thermal fuses as small cylinders on leads in coffee makers, fans and motors; capillary thermostats with a dial in ovens and fridges. Old round wall thermostats hold a glass mercury switch: don’t break it.
test: At room temperature a thermostat or thermal fuse should show continuity. Warm a bimetal disc and it should click open at its rating.
